audit.whatIsWrong: The 2+ items row was given to Kled in both layers, contradicting the packet chart and the page's own why-string, which says Wukong out-scales once armour stacking blunts Kled's on-hit AD.
audit.why: Kled owns levels 2-3 and first item; past two items Wukong's armour and clone tricks beat Kled's frontloaded burst.
audit.corrected: 2+ items flipped to Wukong in both layers; the other six rows already matched the packet.

audit.why: Kled: W at 2, full re-E pattern at 3, R at 6 (140/125/110s), Eclipse first item. Wukong: level 6 and two-plus items of armour.

audit.whatIsWrong: No Wukong ability was named in the full layer (packet defect), and nothing anywhere gives the tell for when his burst starts.
audit.why: Crushing Blow (Q) is an auto-attack reset, so his damage begins on the attack wind-up rather than on a visible cast — that wind-up, not the dash, is the cue to step out of his range. Warrior Trickster (W) leaves the decoy that eats Kled's Beartrap yank and re-E return.
audit.corrected: Crushing Blow and Warrior Trickster named, with the reset tell, in the cooldown and interaction fields.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early, mid and late prose is written in first person ('I respect Skaarl's health bar', '2-3 is mine', 'my remount') — the rest of the site is second person.
audit.why: Voice inconsistency on three of the longest fields on the page.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in second person at the same length.

edits.before: - Wukong Nimbus Strike: matchup-defining — His engage dash. Q-pull the follow-up. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Nimbus Strike (E): his engage dash. Beartrap the follow-up, not the dash. - Crushing Blow (Q) is an auto reset — the attack wind-up is the tell, so step back on the wind-up, not the cast. - Warrior Trickster (W): the decoy eats your yank. - Your R: kill windows only.

edits.before: Track Wukong's Nimbus Strike: His engage dash. Q-pull the follow-up. When it is down — Q-pull + W him.
edits.after: Nimbus Strike (E) is his engage. Crushing Blow (Q) is an auto reset, so his burst starts on the wind-up. Bait Warrior Trickster (W) first, then Beartrap the real body and unload W.

edits.before: His engage dash. Q-pull the follow-up. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Nimbus Strike is his gap-close; Crushing Blow follows it as an auto reset. Punish after both.

edits.before: Level 1 is the usual Kled story — no spammable poke, so I respect Skaarl's health bar and farm rather than feed his Q armor-shred autos. Then 2-3 is mine: W gives me the on-hit shotgun shots and the full re-E comes online, so I E through him, fire W procs, throw the Q trap and yank myself back in, then re-E for the bonus return strike before his clone or shred can answer. The trap I watch for is his W clone — if he flickers it out I can dump my whole combo into a decoy, so bait it before I commit my real all-in.
edits.after: Level 1 is the usual Kled story — no spammable poke, so respect Skaarl's health bar and farm rather than feed Crushing Blow's armor-shred autos. Then 2-3 is yours: W gives you the on-hit shotgun shots and the full re-E comes online, so E through him, fire W procs, throw the Q trap and yank yourself back in, then re-E for the bonus return strike before his clone or shred can answer. Watch for Warrior Trickster (W) — if he flickers it out you dump the whole combo into a decoy, so bait it before you commit the real all-in.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 stay roughly even — I keep stacking W procs and remount sustain, but his Q armor-shred plus E-dash and clone give him real trade-back, so I don't swing blind. At 6 my R can knock him into a wall and stick the all-in, but his R spin-knockup will interrupt my Chaaaaaaaaarge mid-flight if I telegraph it, so I charge when his R is down or after I bait it. Hit the clone, not the man, and force the trade while my mount health is topped off.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 stay roughly even — you keep stacking W procs and remount sustain, but Crushing Blow's armor-shred plus Nimbus Strike and the clone give him real trade-back, so don't swing blind. At 6 your R can knock him into a wall and stick the all-in, but Cyclone's spin-knockup interrupts your Chaaaaaaaaarge mid-flight if you telegraph it, so charge when his R is down or after you bait it. Bait the clone first, and force the trade while mount health is topped off.

edits.before: My first-item Eclipse/Trinity proc and percent-HP Q are my peak, so I want this lane closed on short trades before two items. After that it tilts to him: he stacks armor that my on-hit AD shots scale poorly into, his W clone keeps baiting my re-E into nothing, and his R reset and bruiser DPS out-fight me the instant my remount is on cooldown. So I snowball the 2-3 and first-item windows or this flattens into his favor — and if it goes long I pick my all-ins around his W and R cooldowns instead of stat-checking him.
edits.after: Your first-item Eclipse/Trinity proc and percent-HP Q are your peak, so close this lane on short trades before two items. After that it tilts to him: he stacks armor your on-hit AD shots scale poorly into, Warrior Trickster keeps baiting your re-E into nothing, and his R reset and bruiser DPS out-fight you the instant your remount is on cooldown. So snowball the 2-3 and first-item windows or this flattens into his favor — and if it goes long, pick your all-ins around his W and R cooldowns instead of stat-checking him.

notes: The Wukong kit file was null in the brief (enemyKit: null), so no Wukong cooldown numbers could be verified and none were written — ability names come from packet.enemyAbilities and the missing-interaction record only. Two real issues fixed: the 2+ items row contradicted the packet and the page's own why-string, and early/mid/late were written in first person against the site's second-person voice.
